exposure: first trimester vaginal bleeding (any, severe, prolonged (>1 week), initial episode timing 5-12 weeks gestation, initial episode timing within 4 weeks gestation, mild, within 1 week)
cohort: The study included 10,179 pregnant women in Lanzhou, China.
finding: Vaginal bleeding in the first trimester was an independent risk factor for preterm birth, with its severity, duration, and initial timing having varying effects on different subtypes of preterm birth.
